text: The 2007 Special Olympics World Summer Games (Chinese: 2007年世界夏季特殊奥林匹克运动会; pinyin: 2007 Nián shìjiè xiàjì tèshū àolínpǐkè yùndònghuì) took place in Shanghai, China. During the games, The Special Olympics officially launched Young Athletes, a sports program for children aged 2–7 with intellectual disabilities, following its pilot run in 2006. The program aimed to introduce these children to sports and foster interest before they become eligible to compete in the Special Olympics. It was tested in 11 other countries and involved over 10,000 children. The event generated a total of $101,663,833 in revenue, gains, and other financial support, representing a $16,898,416 increase from the previous year. Total expenses amounted to $101,010,125, an increase of $19,841,738 compared to 2006. Two weeks after the closing ceremony on October 23, Special Olympics founder Eunice Kennedy Shriver was awarded the Minerva Award for Lifetime Achievement. The award, named after the Roman goddess Minerva, recognizes women who have driven change in their communities, states, and nations, and was given in appreciation of Shriver’s contributions to the Special Olympics and her broader efforts to support people with disabilities.
